mandate: Hephaestus alone is responsible for validating that a fully-specified proposed order construction is exactly what strategy-definition-v1.0.md commands for this trigger: the entry limit price reproduces from the ACTIVE §5.3 variant (entry.variant) using raw snapshot values; the stop sits structurally beyond the trigger wick extreme in the adverse direction and is not widened at birth (§5.4); the target is the §6 selection-tree output from the snapshot's target_menu (pattern defaults §6.2, news-day override §6.3, front-run working price §6.4, alignment preference §6.6); the RR floor gates the trade to SKIP when the nearest valid target pays less than targets.rr_floor of the recomputed R (§6.5); the full/half unit call matches the §9 conviction formula recomputed from raw trigger/indicator fields; and the whole construction is internally coherent (direction-consistent ordering stop<entry<target for longs, mirrored for shorts, every price tick-aligned to instrument.tick_size). Hephaestus re-derives every number independently from Snapshot+Trigger+config — it is the cross-check that catches engine bugs (e.g. the displacement entry_ref=first-penetrated-level vs §5.3 E3 nearest-to-close discrepancy found in triggers.py) and stale config. It does NOT judge whether the setup itself is valid (Apollo), whether structure/levels are right (Atlas), or whether the session/news context permits trading (Helios); it takes trigger fields like confluence_count and htf_flag as given inputs to the §9 formula without re-litigating them. It proposes and grades; it never places, sizes in dollars, or transmits anything — the Vault owns execution and risk ceilings.
strategy_slice_refs: §3 (verbatim: rejection-block + tradeable-zone-wick definition, displacement definition, over-extension = touch of NY VWAP ±2σ)
§5 items 3–6 (verbatim: E1/E2/E3 limit variants, stop beyond wick extreme / displacement origin never widened, no-chase T_cancel, one position)
§6 entire (verbatim: target menu, selection tree v1 incl. §6.3 news-day override, §6.4 front-run F, §6.5 RR floor, §6.6 alignment bonus)
§9 (verbatim: sizing & conviction — full vs half unit formula)
§11 (verbatim: architecture boundary — agents grade and propose; Python owns sizing, stops, limits, execution)

checks.name: entry_matches_active_variant
checks.pass_condition: Recompute E per config entry.variant — E1: E = indicators.tfs[trigger.tf].bb_basis; E2: E = (trigger.wick_low + trigger.wick_high) / 2 (the §3 tradeable zone: body edge to wick extreme, exactly what wick_low/wick_high encode); E3: E = price of the penetrated cluster member nearest trigger.close, resolved by mapping clusters[].members names to indicator values (bb_basis_{tf} → indicators.tfs[tf].bb_basis, dvwap_* → indicators.daily_vwap.*, nyvwap_* → indicators.ny_vwap.*, poc → indicators.daily_profile.poc). PASS iff proposed.entry == round_to_tick(E) exactly. Any required input null (e.g. bb_basis None for trigger TF) → FAIL.
checks.fail_note: Entry limit does not reproduce from the active §5.3 variant — engine bug, stale entry.variant config, or the known triggers.py E3 discrepancy (entry_ref = first-penetrated level, not nearest-to-close).

checks.name: stop_beyond_wick_extreme
checks.pass_condition: Long: proposed.stop <= trigger.wick_low AND (trigger.wick_low − proposed.stop) <= instrument.tick_size AND proposed.stop < proposed.entry. Short: proposed.stop >= trigger.wick_high AND (proposed.stop − trigger.wick_high) <= instrument.tick_size AND proposed.stop > proposed.entry. Additionally |proposed.stop − round_to_tick(trigger.stop_ref)| <= instrument.tick_size (stop is structural at/just beyond the wick extreme or displacement origin — never widened at construction).
checks.fail_note: Stop is not structurally placed at/just beyond the trigger wick extreme in the adverse direction, or has been widened relative to stop_ref.

checks.name: target_is_pattern_default
checks.pass_condition: Restrict target_menu to levels strictly beyond proposed.entry in trade direction (long: price > entry; short: price < entry). Recompute the §6.2 default: pattern A → VWAP middle (ny_vwap_mid if indicators.ny_vwap.mid is non-null, else daily_vwap_mid); B2 → nearest menu level beyond entry in the move direction; B → nearest opposing-liquidity level among {premarket/Asia/London session extremes, prior_day_high/low} beyond entry, preferring a candidate within cluster.tolerance_points of indicators.ny_vwap.upper_2/lower_2 when one exists. PASS iff proposed.target_name exists in target_menu AND proposed.target_level == that menu level's price AND it equals the recomputed default (unless check news_day_override_applied legitimately overrides it). A proposed target not present in target_menu → FAIL unconditionally.
checks.fail_note: Chosen target is not the §6.2 selection-tree default for this pattern, or is not a menu level at all.

checks.name: news_day_override_applied
checks.pass_condition: If targets.news_day_override is true AND there exists a data_levels entry with impact == high whose extreme in trade direction (long: data_high; short: data_low) lies strictly beyond the check-3 default target AND is untaken (long: data_high >= snapshot.session_high; short: data_low <= snapshot.session_low), then PASS iff proposed.target_level equals the nearest such data extreme; otherwise PASS iff proposed target equals the check-3 default (vacuous pass when no qualifying extreme or override disabled). If targets.news_override_vwap_proxy is true, substitute the VWAP −1/+1 proxy per config instead of the data extreme.
checks.fail_note: News-day target override was skipped when a qualifying untaken high-impact data extreme exists (or was applied when it should not have been).

checks.name: front_run_working_target
checks.pass_condition: Long: proposed.working_target == round_to_tick(proposed.target_level − targets.front_run_points). Short: proposed.working_target == round_to_tick(proposed.target_level + targets.front_run_points). And working_target remains strictly beyond proposed.entry in trade direction.
checks.fail_note: Working target does not equal target level ∓ F points, or front-running collapsed the target to/behind entry.

checks.name: rr_floor_met
checks.pass_condition: R = |proposed.entry − proposed.stop| > 0 AND (|proposed.working_target − proposed.entry| / R) >= targets.rr_floor. If no target satisfying the §6.2/§6.3 tree also clears the floor, the only passing Hephaestus verdict is FAIL with skip_reason 'rr_floor' — a construction proposing the trade anyway must be vetoed. R == 0 (entry equals stop) → FAIL.
checks.fail_note: Nearest valid target pays less than the RR floor — §6.5 commands SKIP, not a thinner trade.

checks.name: size_matches_conviction
checks.pass_condition: target_r = |proposed.working_target − proposed.entry| / |proposed.entry − proposed.stop|. a_at_extension = (trigger.pattern == 'A') AND directional NY VWAP ±2σ touch (long: trigger.wick_low <= indicators.ny_vwap.lower_2; short: trigger.wick_high >= indicators.ny_vwap.upper_2; both bands non-null — pre-09:30 NY VWAP is null so a_at_extension is false). full_ok = (trigger.confluence_count >= sizing.full_unit_min_confluences) AND (trigger.htf_flag == 'with_trend' OR a_at_extension) AND (target_r >= sizing.full_unit_min_target_r). half_forced = (trigger.confluence_count == 2) OR oversized_stop OR late_window OR (target_r < sizing.full_unit_min_target_r); while oversized_stop and late_window lack config definitions (see open questions) they evaluate as INDETERMINATE, and any proposed size 'full' under an indeterminate half-condition FAILS (fail-closed to half). PASS iff proposed.size == ('full' if full_ok AND NOT half_forced else 'half').
checks.fail_note: Proposed unit size does not reproduce from the §9 conviction formula — includes the fail-closed case where 'full' is claimed while a half-condition is indeterminate.

checks.name: construction_coherent_and_tick_aligned
checks.pass_condition: proposed.direction == trigger.direction; long: proposed.stop < proposed.entry < proposed.working_target <= proposed.target_level; short: proposed.target_level <= proposed.working_target < proposed.entry < proposed.stop; each of proposed.entry, proposed.stop, proposed.working_target is an exact multiple of instrument.tick_size; proposed.size ∈ {'full','half'}; all prices finite and > 0.
checks.fail_note: Construction is internally incoherent: wrong direction, price ordering violated, or a price is not tick-aligned to 0.25.

checks.name: target_alignment_preference
checks.pass_condition: PASS iff no alternative target_menu level beyond proposed.entry in trade direction exists that (a) belongs to the same §6.2 pattern-default family and clears targets.rr_floor, (b) has >= targets.alignment_min_stack menu levels stacked within cluster.tolerance_points of it while the chosen target has fewer, and (c) is nearer to entry than the chosen target or equal in tree rank. Ties between equally-stacked candidates are a judgment call and must be explained in the gate note; an unexplained bypass of a better-stacked valid target FAILS.
checks.fail_note: A valid target with a stronger §6.6 level stack (or §6.2 ±2σ alignment for B) was bypassed without justification.

agent_version.description: Version stamp of hephaestus.md — prompt edits are versioned like code (ai-workflow-rules).

trigger_ts.description: Echo of Trigger.ts (ISO ET) — join key for Hermes; guards against grading a stale candidate.

verdict.description: fail = veto. Any gate false, any required input null, or any recompute mismatch forces fail. Hermes must also treat missing/late/invalid-JSON output as fail (fail-closed).

recomputed.description: Hephaestus's independent re-derivation — Hermes compares these to the engine's proposed construction; any mismatch is itself evidence of an engine bug and must be logged.

skip_reasons.description: Machine-readable veto reasons for the Vault's strict-schema journal (§10).

thesis.description: Human-auditable one-paragraph construction rationale: which variant produced the entry, why this target per the §6 tree, the R math, and the §9 size call. No P&L, no history, no confidence scores.

edge_cases: E1 with indicators.tfs[trigger.tf].bb_basis null (insufficient history at session start) — no entry price derivable → verdict fail with skip_reason missing_input, never a fallback to another variant.

Pre-09:30 candidate: indicators.ny_vwap.* all null → pattern-A default 'VWAP middle' resolves to daily_vwap_mid (§3 pre-9:30 VWAP family = daily only, architecture invariant 1), A-at-extension is unachievable so full unit requires with_trend, and B-pattern ±2σ alignment preference is vacuous.

Displacement trigger: 'wick' semantics differ — Trigger encodes wick_low/wick_high as origin-to-body-edge (long: lo→o), so E2's '50% of the trigger candle's wick' rides on that encoding; the displacement candle's full high/low is NOT in the Trigger, so over-extension recompute uses the directional extreme only (long: wick_low IS the candle low; short: wick_high IS the candle high — the opposite side is unavailable and must not be guessed).

E3 on a displacement: engine's entry_ref = min(up_through) (first level penetrated) but §5.3 says level nearest the block's close = max(up_through) for longs — Hephaestus's recompute from clusters[].members will flag every such trade until the discrepancy is ruled on.
Front-run collapse: a near target minus front_run_points lands at or behind entry (working_target <= entry for a long) → construction incoherent → fail, not a zero-R trade.
Target exactly at the floor: target_r_multiple == targets.rr_floor passes (>= is the §6.5 boundary); float comparison needs an epsilon smaller than one tick's R contribution.

Cluster-derived prices (cluster center is a mean, VWAP bands are floats) are not tick-multiples — the proposed construction must be tick-rounded while the recompute compares against round_to_tick(raw); a proposal matching the RAW float but not the tick grid fails coherence, not entry-match.
Multiple qualifying untaken high-impact data extremes beyond the default target → the nearest one in trade direction is the override target; a farther one chosen = fail.
data_high exactly equal to session_high: the extreme IS the session high (printed, never exceeded) → counts as untaken; session_high strictly greater → taken, override does not apply.

Trigger.ts at the last bar of the entry window under W2 (window wraps 18:00→15:55 across midnight): late-window evaluation must use the ACTIVE window variant's clock, tz-aware ET — never offset arithmetic.

ref_price or the entire proposed construction missing/partial (engine handed only entry_ref/stop_ref) → Hephaestus cannot validate what does not exist: fail with skip_reason schema_or_null_input, per fail-closed.
open_questions_for_spec3: WHO COMPUTES THE CONSTRUCTION (flagged per task note): recommend the engine's Step-7 order builder computes the full ProposedConstruction {direction, entry, stop, target_name, target_level, working_target, size} deterministically from config, and Hephaestus validates it — Hermes never computes prices, agents never originate numbers. Spec 3 must pin this and define the ProposedConstruction schema as part of the Engine→Desk contract.

ENGINE DISCREPANCY (found, needs Angus ruling before Phase 3): triggers.py sets displacement entry_ref = min(up_through) for longs (first level penetrated) while §5.3 E3 reads 'penetrated cluster level nearest the block's close' (= max(up_through) for longs). Confirm intended semantics or fix; Hephaestus's E3 recompute will veto every displacement E3 trade until resolved.

STOP CONVENTION: §5.4 says stop 'beyond the wick extreme' but triggers.py places stop_ref AT the extreme (lo/h exactly). Is the stop at the extreme or N ticks beyond? Recommend a config key (e.g. entry.stop_buffer_ticks, § 5.4-traced) so the check is exact instead of the interim ≤1-tick tolerance.

E2 ON DISPLACEMENT: what is 'the trigger candle's wick' for a displacement candle — the origin-to-body-edge zone the Trigger encodes, or the classical wick? Angus to confirm; the Trigger field encoding currently forces the former.

RR FLOOR BASIS: is the §6.5 floor measured to the raw target level or the front-run working target? Recommend working target (matches §6.4's 'backtest counts touched-minus-F as filled') — the checks above assume it; needs Angus confirmation and a comment in strategy.yaml.

§9 UNDEFINED HALF-TRIGGERS: 'oversized stop' and 'late-window entry' have no computable definitions or config keys. Propose sizing.oversized_stop_points (or ATR multiple) and sizing.late_window_start (per entry-window variant); until defined Hephaestus fails any 'full' proposal fail-closed — confirm that behavior is acceptable for calibration.

CLUSTER MEMBER PRICES: Snapshot.Cluster carries member names but not prices, so the E3 recompute relies on name→indicator resolution (dvwap_upper_1 → indicators.daily_vwap.upper_1 etc.). Recommend adding member (name, price, type) tuples to Cluster in snapshot.py so the recompute is direct and name-scheme drift can't silently break it.

'VWAP MIDDLE' FOR PATTERN-A DEFAULT: NY VWAP mid post-09:30 vs daily VWAP mid pre — the doc says only 'VWAP middle'. The design assumes ny_vwap_mid when non-null else daily_vwap_mid (consistent with §3's pre-9:30 rule); Angus to confirm.

'UNTAKEN' DATA EXTREME: confirm the computable definition (data extreme not strictly exceeded by session_high/low since event_time). Cleaner alternative: engine stamps a per-data-level 'swept' boolean into Snapshot.data_levels so the Desk never approximates it.

SIZE VOCABULARY IN THE PINNED VERDICT: recommend Verdict.size is the enum {full, half}, never a contract count — the Vault alone maps units to contracts via the Monte Carlo ceiling (§9/§10). Spec 3 should pin the enum.

TICK-ROUNDING DIRECTION: nearest-tick vs conservative (entry rounded toward stop, target rounded toward entry)? Affects fill realism parity with the backtester; needs one rule in strategy.yaml traced to spec-1 §3.
split_concerns: Three overlaps and one gap. (1) §9 sizing structurally straddles all four lanes: its inputs are confluence count (Atlas's level territory), with-trend flag (Atlas/Apollo), A-at-extension (Apollo's pattern anatomy), and late-window (Helios's clock). Since specialists cannot see each other's verdicts, Hephaestus must re-read the raw fields (trigger.confluence_count, trigger.htf_flag, trigger.pattern, ny_vwap ±2σ vs wick, snapshot.ts) and apply the formula itself — deliberate duplication that preserves independence, but spec 3 must state that Hephaestus takes these trigger fields AS GIVEN for the sizing formula (their verification belongs to Atlas/Apollo/Helios), otherwise every lane re-litigates everything and a single engine value gets four divergent re-derivations with no tiebreak rule. Hermes should log (not arbitrate) any cross-specialist inconsistency as an additional veto reason. (2) The §6.3 news-day override forces Hephaestus into Helios's news lane: 'is there a qualifying high-impact untaken extreme' is target-selection logic (mine) built on news facts (Helios's). The split holds only because data_levels[].impact is raw snapshot data, not a Helios judgment — keep it that way. (3) Over-extension is computed independently by Apollo (pattern-A classification) and Hephaestus (A-at-extension full-unit gate) from the same fields; identical formula must be pinned verbatim in both agent files or the two can disagree on the same candle. GAP: nobody on the Desk owns §5.5 no-chase/T_cancel or §8 management variants — correctly so (they're order-lifecycle mechanics for the engine/Vault), but spec 3 should say this explicitly so the omission reads as designed, not forgotten. Finally, note that Hephaestus's rr_floor fail is semantically a SKIP verdict, not a 'bad construction' — Hermes must map it to the same veto path (fail-closed makes them equivalent downstream, but the journal reason should distinguish skip-by-rule from construction-defect for the §12.5 diagnostics slices).
